question.problem:
The function $f(x)$ is defined for every real number $x$ and is given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14189990/assets/90209edc9ee3cc9c6c17b71427dc4dda0a14558a9df7b2a71dbe017073b9086a.svg)
If $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=1,$ what is the value of $k?$
question.worked_solution:
From the definition of $f(x),$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \,1}({x}^{2}+2kx+1) \\  & ={1}^{2}+2k(1)+1 \\  & =2+2k.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x=1,$ we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}f(x) & =f(1) \\ 2+2k & =4 \\ 2k & =2 \\ k & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, setting $k=1$ removes the point discontinuity.
